title: Zero-shot anchor synthesis and coverage mapper
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

This document defines the Zero-shot Anchor Synthesis (ZAS) framework and the Coverage Mapper component used by the eval harness to generate, score, and track representative anchors for prompt families without requiring task-specific labeled data. ZAS is intended to improve probe coverage, reduce annotation cost, and provide stable coverage signals for quantization and rollout decisions.

Scope

- Applies to: prompt-sets-and-benchmarks, eval-harness integration, model-onboarding shadow validation, and probe stewardship.
- Not in scope: human labeling workflows after anchors are selected (see annotation charters).

Motivation

- Many services lack dense labeled datasets across all prompt families and locales.
- Existing probe sets are biased toward observed failures and miss rare, high-impact tails.
- ZAS synthesizes compact representative prompts that approximate diverse decision boundaries in embedding and behavior space, enabling automated coverage estimation and targeted probe generation.

Key definitions

- Anchor: a short prompt or priming sequence representing a region of runtime distribution for a probe slice.
- Coverage score: numeric estimate of how well anchors represent observed or synthetic workload clusters.
- Probe efficiency: ratio of unique-failure signal rate to tokens or annotation budget spent.

Design overview

Inputs:
- Seed traces: anonymized request samples from shadow or escrowed production traces.
- Heuristics: length buckets, functioncall flags, few-shot template families.
- Model fingerprints: embeddings from a reference embedder, tokenization profiles, and simple KV cache proxies.

Zero-shot synthesis pipeline (high level):
1) Preprocess and redact seeds.
2) Cluster seeds using the reference embedder and a silhouette stopping threshold.
3) For each cluster generate candidate anchors with multiple generators: paraphrase sampler, contrastive prompt builder, and a minimalizer that produces concise variants.
4) Score candidates with an ensemble of signals: embedding centrality, behavior diversity measured by response entropy across a small ensemble, and brevity penalty.
5) Pick top-K candidates per cluster and deduplicate with a lightweight reranker.

Coverage Mapper responsibilities

- Maintain an index of anchors with fields: anchor id, canonical text, cluster id, embedding, last seen timestamp, and a coverage histogram.
- Match live or shadow requests to nearest anchors and update histograms in streaming windows.
- Emit weekly coverage reports and a Coverage Gap list for low-match but high-hinterland similarity anchors.

Exposed configuration parameters

- E_ref: reference embedding model name used for clustering (default: rwd-embed-large-v1).
- T_s: silhouette threshold for clustering stop (default: 0.48).
- K: number of anchors selected per cluster (default: 3).
- sim_match: cosine threshold used to consider a request matched to an anchor (default: 0.82).
- entropy_weight: relative weight for the response-entropy signal during scoring (default: 0.4).

Operational SLOs and metrics

- Anchor generation latency for a 10k-seed job: median < 90s, p95 < 300s.
- Coverage index freshness for streaming updates: <= 5 minutes.
- Coverage completeness target: 0.85 coverage ratio for high-volume slices within 7 days.
- Probe efficiency uplift goal: +25% unique-failures-per-token compared to baseline probe sampler after 30 days.

Scoring heuristics

- Embedding centrality: mean cosine similarity to cluster members, normalized to 0..1.
- Behavior diversity: entropy across outputs from three model checkpoints normalized by max entropy.
- Brevity: exponential penalty to prefer concise prompts.
- Composite score: weighted sum, default weights: 0.5 centrality, 0.4 entropy_norm, 0.1 brevity.

Anchor lifecycle and provenance

- Anchors are created with a provenance record capturing seed cluster, generator type, generation timestamp, and config hash.
- States: proposed -> validated -> active -> retired.
- Validation criteria: manual curator approval or statistical evidence of coverage match within a short validation window.

Operator procedure: running a scheduled ZAS job

1) Prepare an anonymized seed bundle and upload to the seed bucket.
2) Launch synthesis with the job control CLI and reference config.
3) Monitor job metrics in Grafana under EvalHarness and watch anchor generation latency alerts.
4) Run the built-in validation sampler and push candidates for curator review if required.

Example minimal configuration (YAML style):
- embedder: rwd-embed-large-v1
- clusterer: recommended method hdbscan with silhouette_thresh 0.48
- generators: paraphrase-sampler, contrastive-prompt-builder, minimalizer
- scoring: entropy_weight 0.4, brevity_lambda 0.02
- selection: top_k 3

Integration points with eval harness and onboarding

- The Coverage Mapper offers a REST endpoint /coverage/match for the eval harness to annotate probes during shadow runs.
- Onboarding checklist for a new service:
  1) Register the service namespace and owner metadata in the coverage index.
  2) Provide a seed bundle with at least 5k anonymized traces and a short list of high-sensitivity slices.
  3) Run ZAS and validate top-K anchors per slice.
  4) Add anchors to the eval schedule and allocate an initial probe-burst budget for two weeks.

Curator and reviewer guidelines

- Prioritize anchors with high composite score and low current probe coverage.
- Reject anchors that contain or reveal sensitive identifiers, even if synthetic.
- If ambiguous, add an intent label and a short example context to the provenance record.

Common failure modes and mitigations

- Anchor collapse: many clusters yield near-identical anchors. Mitigation: increase silhouette threshold, raise minimum cluster size, and deduplicate via cross-encoder.
- PII leakage: seeds expose identifiers that survive redaction. Mitigation: stronger redaction, add noise during paraphrase generation, enable curator gating for high-risk slices.
- Drift in embeddings: match recall degrades after embedder updates. Mitigation: scheduled weekly re-embedding and threshold recalibration using a holdout window.

Dashboards and reporting

- Grafana panels: anchors_by_slice, coverage_ratio_7d, anchor_match_latency, probe_efficiency_delta.
- Weekly digest email: top 10 coverage gaps and recommended probe generation actions.

Ownership and runbooks

- Owner: Applied ML - Probe Platform team (eng-applied-ml@redwood.com).
- Primary oncall: Applied ML oncall rotation.
- Runbooks: anchor index recovery and job troubleshooting runbooks in the Applied ML runbook repository.

Human-in-the-loop sampling heuristics

- For limited annotation budgets, use stratified-uncertainty sampling: half sampling equally across clusters and half proportional to composite score.
- Allocate a minimum of 200 human checks per high-impact slice in the first month after anchor activation.

Planned work and roadmap notes

- Multilingual anchor generators using bilingual pivoting for low-resource languages.
- Lightweight local cross-encoders on edge to improve matching for short prompts and functioncall-heavy contexts.

Contact and next steps

If you want to pilot ZAS for a service, file a request in the Applied ML probe backlog and tag the request with zas-pilot. For questions, ping the author or the Applied ML team alias.
